Everything else is a recording. Read the last section before relying on it."},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## The part that is actually reusable: reconstructing a replay correctly

Before any of this can be measured, one detail has to be right, and it is easy to get wrong.

In a Kaggle replay, `steps[t]["action"]` is the action an agent produced **from observation
`t-1`** â€” it is stored next to the state it led to, not the state it was chosen from. So the
action a replayer must play at `obs["step"] == t` lives at **`steps[t+1]["action"]`**.

Get this wrong and nothing errors. The replay just runs a turn late: it walks to where the crop
*was*, buys the seed a turn after it was needed, sells into a market that already moved. The
season still completes, so there is no failure to notice.

The test is exact and costs one episode: rebuild both seats of a replay you already have and
check that re-running them reproduces the recorded final banks **exactly**. On the ten episodes
I checked, the shifted reconstruction is 10/10 byte-exact and the unshifted is 0/10.

That single fix reversed the sign of a result for me. I had rejected an entire route family on
evidence gathered against desynchronised opponents; corrected, that family beat the agent I had
kept."},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"# Also worth checking before you trust any local number: the notebook image and

I would rather publish the limits than the score.

**A recorded tape has no exploitable slack.** I spent a long time trying to add work to one and
failed in three distinct ways. Its empty tiles are not idle â€” they are reserved for later builds,
and planting in them cost animals and crops. Its `PASS` turns are not idle either â€” they hold a
unit in place for a later recorded action, and moving that unit breaks the choreography
downstream. And its cash is fully committed, so anything you buy starves something it planned.
Every apparent spare resource is spare only because the recording assumes it stays that way.

**A better-banking tape is not a better tape.** Ranking ten recorded episodes from the same
strong team by their solo throughput, and separately by head-to-head record against that same
team, gives two nearly unrelated orders. The episode I ended up using is one its author *lost*.
A tape records how someone played against a particular opponent, and their play under pressure
from a strong rival is their strongest recorded play. If you select a tape by its final bank you
will probably pick the wrong one.

**Local dominance does not imply ladder transfer.** I have a candidate that beats this one 30-0
on thirty fresh preregistered seeds in both seats, with a familywise-corrected Wilson bound, zero
errors â€” every statistical box ticked. On the live ladder it currently scores *lower*. Thirty
paired seeds against three baselines is a real measurement and it still did not predict the
result, because the local panel is not the ladder population.

**And the ceiling is structural.** This artifact scores 2948.9 while the team whose route it
replays sits above it. Cloning caps out below the thing being cloned, because what is missing is
precisely the part that reacted. If you are here to win rather than to place, the tape is a
baseline to beat, not a destination â€” and that is the honest reason I am publishing it rather
than guarding it."}],"metadata":{"kernelspec":{"display_name":"Python 3","language":"python","name":"python3"},"language_info":{"name":"python","version":"3.11"}},"nbformat":4,"nbformat_minor":5}

Everything else is a recording. Read the last section before relying on it."},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## The part that is actually reusable: reconstructing a replay correctly

Before any of this can be measured, one detail has to be right, and it is easy to get wrong.

In a Kaggle replay, `steps[t]["action"]` is the action an agent produced **from observation
`t-1`** â€” it is stored next to the state it led to, not the state it was chosen from. So the
action a replayer must play at `obs["step"] == t` lives at **`steps[t+1]["action"]`**.

Get this wrong and nothing errors. The replay just runs a turn late: it walks to where the crop
*was*, buys the seed a turn after it was needed, sells into a market that already moved. The
season still completes, so there is no failure to notice.

I checked, the shifted reconstruction is 10/10 byte-exact and the unshifted is 0/10.
